CoreOS is part of 4 of my public repositories, from 2014 to 2025.

What it was for: [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (3) and [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1).

Most recently: [microcrawler](@/work/microcrawler.md); [server-coreos](@/work/server-coreos.md): CoreOS based immutable server; [cluster](@/work/cluster.md): Run your own CoreOS/Kubernetes cluster.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses CoreOS: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links CoreOS to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
